title: Wallet binding
subtitle: A Coptic-sewn text block whose boards extend into a foredge closure flap
excerpt: A wallet binding extends one cover board past the foredge and folds it over the text block to close the book. The flap tucks under a narrow leather or cloth strap on the front cover. The design goes back to medieval document cases and is well suited to sketchbooks and travel journals.
sourceNotes: Cyril Davenport, The Book: Its History and Development (1907), on medieval wallet and chemise binding forms. Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (1901), on cover construction and closure systems.

glossaryTerms.definition: The extension of the back cover board past the foredge of the text block, which folds over the front to close the book.

content.text: A wallet binding is a Coptic or long-stitch sewn text block whose back board extends 40 to 50 mm past the foredge as a

. When closed, the flap folds over the front cover and tucks under a strap glued to the front board. The style suits a sketchbook or travel journal: it protects the foredge better than a flush cover and the flap gives a natural surface to grip when carrying the book in a bag.

attrs.heading: Cutting tools safety
attrs.body: Sharp blades are safer than blunt blades. Cut on a self-healing cutting mat. Keep the non-cutting hand at least two finger-widths from the blade path.

items.name: Bookbinding board, 2 mm
items.notes: Front board: cut 5 mm larger than text block on three sides (head, tail, foredge). Back board: cut the same on head and tail, but 50 mm larger on the foredge to form the wallet flap.

items.name: Book cloth or decorated paper
items.notes: For covering the boards. The flap must flex, so use cloth or a thin, flexible paper rather than stiff card.

items.name: Leather strap, 10 mm wide, 60 mm long
items.notes: Or a strip of cloth glued to the front board to form the closure loop. The flap tucks under this strap when the book is closed.

items.name: PVA, acid-free
items.notes: For gluing the strap to the front board and the covering cloth to the boards.

items.name: Bone folder
items.notes: For pressing covered boards flat while drying.

content.text: Cut the front board at 5 mm larger on head, tail, and foredge (standard square for A5 format: 155 x 220 mm). Cut the back board to 155 mm tall and 198 mm wide (148 mm text block width plus 50 mm wallet flap). Cover both boards in book cloth, wrapping the turn-ins neatly. Score the flap fold-line on the back board 148 mm from the spine edge with the bone folder: the flap must flex at this line without cracking the board. If the board resists, score more firmly or dampen the score line very slightly before folding.

Cut the strap to 60 mm. Apply PVA to the first 15 mm of the strap and glue it to the centre of the front board's foredge, positioned so the free 45 mm hangs over the foredge when the board lies flat. The strap forms a loop: when the book is closed and the wallet flap folds over, the flap tip slides under the strap. Allow the strap adhesion to dry for an hour under a small weight before sewing.
Sew the text block into the boards

Sew the text block with a Coptic or long-stitch sewn directly through the boards at the spine edge. Pierce the boards at matching station positions with the bookbinding awl. Sew exactly as for a standard Coptic binding, working a

at the head and tail of each signature. The boards now carry the text block as covers. When the book is closed, test the wallet flap: it should fold over the front cleanly and the tip should tuck under the strap with light pressure.

The scored fold-line on the wallet flap will soften with use and eventually crease cleanly. If the cloth covering at the score line starts to crack, reinforce it from inside with a 15 mm strip of Japanese tissue applied with wheat paste.
